def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--story", type=int, default=1, help="1-based index into the QuALITY dev split")
    ap.add_argument("-q", "--question", type=int, action="append", help="1-based question numbers")
    ap.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument(
        "--build", action="store_true", help="build the story's tree if it does not exist"
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()

    story = load_quality("dev", limit=args.story)[-1]
    tree_dir = TREES / f"quality_story_{args.story}_gemini"
    models = models_for(tree_dir)
    cfg = RaptorConfig()
    cfg.chunking.max_tokens = 250
    cfg.builder.max_layers = 3

    if tree_dir.exists():
        ra = RetrievalAugmentation(
            cfg,
            tree=tree_dir,
            embedding_model=models.embedding,
            summarization_model=models.summarization,
            qa_model=models.qa,
        )
    elif args.build:
        ra = RetrievalAugmentation(
            cfg,
            embedding_model=models.embedding,
            summarization_model=models.summarization,
            qa_model=models.qa,
        )
        ra.add_documents(story.article)
        ra.save(tree_dir)
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"{tree_dir} not found; pass --build to create it")

    assert ra.tree is not None
    flat = FlatRAG.from_tree(ra.tree, models.embedding, models.qa, top_k=args.top_k)
    print(
        f"'{story.title}' ({story.word_count} words): {len(ra.tree.leaf_nodes)} leaves, "
        f"{len(ra.tree.all_nodes)} nodes, top layer {ra.tree.num_layers}\n"
    )

    numbers = args.question or list(range(1, len(story.questions) + 1))
    score = {"flat": 0, "raptor": 0}
    for n in numbers:
        q = story.questions[n - 1]
        prompt = q.mcq_prompt()
        flat_ctx, _ = flat.retrieve(q.question)
        flat_ans = models.qa.answer_question(flat_ctx, prompt)
        res = ra.retrieve_nodes(q.question, top_k=args.top_k)
        raptor_ans = models.qa.answer_question(res.context, prompt)
        fp, rp = predicted_option(flat_ans), predicted_option(raptor_ans)
        score["flat"] += fp == q.gold_label
        score["raptor"] += rp == q.gold_label
        print(
            f"Q{n}: {q.question}\n  gold={q.gold_label}  flat={fp}  raptor={rp}  "
            f"raptor layers={res.layer_counts()}"
        )
    print(
        f"\nAccuracy over {len(numbers)} questions: flat {score['flat']}/{len(numbers)}, "
        f"raptor {score['raptor']}/{len(numbers)}"
    )

def build_from_chunks(
        self,
        chunks: Sequence[Chunk],
        *,
        leaf_embeddings: np.ndarray | None = None,
        progress: ProgressCallback | None = None,
    ) -> Tree:
        progress = progress or _noop
        key = self.config.builder.embedding_key
        progress({"stage": "embedding", "layer": 0, "total": len(chunks)})
        if leaf_embeddings is None:
            leaf_embeddings = self.embedding_model.embed_documents([c.text for c in chunks])
        leaves = []
        for i, (chunk, emb) in enumerate(zip(chunks, leaf_embeddings, strict=True)):
            meta = dict(chunk.metadata)
            if chunk.start is not None:
                meta.update(start=chunk.start, end=chunk.end)
            leaves.append(
                Node(chunk.text, i, set(), {key: np.asarray(emb, dtype=np.float32)}, 0, meta)
            )
        logger.info("Created %d leaf nodes", len(leaves))

        layer_to_nodes: dict[int, list[Node]] = {0: leaves}
        current = leaves
        next_index = len(leaves)
        for layer in range(1, self.config.builder.max_layers + 1):
            if len(current) <= self.config.stop_threshold:
                logger.info(
                    "Stopping at layer %d: %d nodes <= %d",
                    layer - 1,
                    len(current),
                    self.config.stop_threshold,
                )
                break
            new_nodes = self._build_layer(current, layer, next_index, progress)
            if len(new_nodes) >= len(current):
                logger.info(
                    "Stopping at layer %d: clustering did not reduce the node count", layer - 1
                )
                break
            layer_to_nodes[layer] = new_nodes
            next_index += len(new_nodes)
            current = new_nodes

        tree = Tree.from_layers(
            layer_to_nodes,
            metadata={
                "embedding_key": key,
                "embedding_model": self.embedding_model.model_id,
                "summarization_model": self.summarization_model.model_id,
                "config": self.config.model_dump(mode="json"),
            },
        )
        progress({"stage": "done", "num_nodes": len(tree.all_nodes), "num_layers": tree.num_layers})
        return tree

def _token_windows(self, text: str, start: int, end: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]:
        tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text[start:end], disallowed_special=())
        out = []
        offset = start
        for i in range(0, len(tokens), self.max_tokens):
            piece = self.tokenizer.decode(tokens[i : i + self.max_tokens])
            # Map decoded piece back onto the source (decoding can normalise bytes).
            found = text.find(piece, offset, end) if piece else -1
            s = found if found >= 0 else offset
            e = min(end, s + len(piece))
            if e > s:
                out.append((s, e, len(tokens[i : i + self.max_tokens])))
            offset = e
        return out

symbols.text:
def split(self, text: str) -> list[Chunk]:
        units = self._units(text)
        chunks: list[Chunk] = []
        current: list[tuple[int, int, int]] = []
        length = 0
        for unit in units:
            if current and length + unit[2] > self.max_tokens:
                chunks.append(self._make(text, current))
                current = self._overlap_tail(current)
                length = sum(u[2] for u in current)
                # The carried tail plus this unit might still not fit; drop tail if so.
                if length + unit[2] > self.max_tokens:
                    current, length = [], 0
            current.append(unit)
            length += unit[2]
        if current:
            chunks.append(self._make(text, current))
        return chunks

def __init__(
        self,
        max_tokens: int = 100,
        overlap_tokens: int = 0,
        tokenizer: tiktoken.Encoding | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if max_tokens < 1 or not 0 <= overlap_tokens < max_tokens:
            raise ValueError("need max_tokens >= 1 and 0 <= overlap_tokens < max_tokens")
        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        self.overlap_tokens = overlap_tokens
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer or default_tokenizer()

symbols.name: split
symbols.text:
def split(self, text: str) -> list[Chunk]:
        tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text, disallowed_special=())
        if not tokens:
            return []
        decoded, offsets = self.tokenizer.decode_with_offsets(tokens)
        if decoded != text:  # pragma: no cover - only for text tiktoken cannot round-trip
            step = self.max_tokens - self.overlap_tokens
            pieces = (
                self.tokenizer.decode(tokens[i : i + self.max_tokens]).strip()
                for i in range(0, len(tokens), step)
            )
            return [Chunk(p) for p in pieces if p]
        n = len(tokens)
        bounds = [*offsets, len(text)]
        chunks: list[Chunk] = []
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = min(i + self.max_tokens, n)
            span = _trim(text, bounds[i], bounds[j])
            # Trimming can change how the edges tokenize; shrink the window until it fits.
            while span and j > i + 1 and self._count(text[span[0] : span[1]]) > self.max_tokens:
                j -= 1
                span = _trim(text, bounds[i], bounds[j])
            if span:
                chunks.append(Chunk(text[span[0] : span[1]], span[0], span[1]))
            if j >= n:
                break
            i = max(j - self.overlap_tokens, i + 1)
        return chunks

Split where the embedding similarity between neighbouring sentences drops.

``overlap_tokens`` is ignored: segments follow topic shifts, not a sliding window.

Breakpoints are the gaps whose cosine distance is above the ``breakpoint_percentile``

segments shorter than ``min_tokens`` are merged into a neighbour.

class SemanticChunker(SentenceChunker):
    """Split where the embedding similarity between neighbouring sentences drops.

    ``overlap_tokens`` is ignored: segments follow topic shifts, not a sliding window.

    Breakpoints are the gaps whose cosine distance is above the ``breakpoint_percentile``
    of all gaps. Segments longer than ``max_tokens`` are re-packed by sentences, and
    segments shorter than ``min_tokens`` are merged into a neighbour.
    """

parsed.module_docstring:
The RAPTOR clustering algorithm: UMAP reduction + Gaussian mixture, global then local.

1. Reduce embeddings with UMAP using a wide neighbourhood (global structure) and fit
   a GMM whose component count minimises BIC. Soft-assign each point to every
   component with probability above ``threshold``.
2. Within each global cluster, repeat with a narrow neighbourhood (local structure).
3. Any resulting cluster whose text exceeds ``max_cluster_tokens`` is re-clustered.

Fixes over the original implementation: seeded UMAP (reproducible trees), direct index
tracking instead of an O(n²·d) equality search (which also mis-mapped duplicate
chunks), parameters preserved through recursion, guarded small-n cases, and a
termination guarantee when an oversized cluster cannot be split further.

symbols.text:
def _umap(embeddings: np.ndarray, dim: int, n_neighbors: int, random_state: int) -> np.ndarray:
    import umap  # imported lazily: numba JIT makes the import slow

    n = len(embeddings)
    n_neighbors = max(2, min(n_neighbors, n - 1))
    dim = max(1, min(dim, n - 2))
    kwargs = {}
    if "compatibility_layout" in inspect.signature(umap.UMAP.__init__).parameters:
        kwargs["compatibility_layout"] = True  # keep the 0.5.x layout the paper used
    reducer = umap.UMAP(
        n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
        n_components=dim,
        metric="cosine",
        random_state=random_state,
        n_jobs=1,
        **kwargs,
    )
    return np.asarray(reducer.fit_transform(embeddings), dtype=np.float64)

symbols.docstring: Soft-assign rows of ``x`` to GMM components. Returns clusters of row indices.
symbols.text:
def _gmm_soft(
    x: np.ndarray, threshold: float, max_clusters: int, random_state: int
) -> list[list[int]]:
    """Soft-assign rows of ``x`` to GMM components. Returns clusters of row indices."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    n_comp = _optimal_components(x, max_clusters, random_state)
    gm = _fit_gmm(x, n_comp, random_state)
    if gm is None:  # even one component failed: treat everything as one cluster
        return [list(range(len(x)))]
    probs = gm.predict_proba(x)
    clusters: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(n_comp)]
    for row, p in enumerate(probs):
        labels = np.where(p > threshold)[0]
        if len(labels) == 0:  # keep every point somewhere
            labels = np.array([int(np.argmax(p))])
        for label in labels:
            clusters[int(label)].append(row)
    return [c for c in clusters if c]

symbols.text:
def _two_level(self, emb: np.ndarray) -> list[np.ndarray]:
        """Global-then-local clustering of ``emb``; returns clusters of local row indices."""
        n = len(emb)
        dim = self.reduction_dimension
        if n <= 3:  # too few points for UMAP; the caller splits further if needed
            return [np.arange(n)]
        neighbors = self.global_neighbors or int((n - 1) ** 0.5)
        reduced = _umap(emb, dim, neighbors, self.random_state)
        global_clusters = _gmm_soft(reduced, self.threshold, self.max_clusters, self.random_state)

        out: list[np.ndarray] = []
        for g in global_clusters:
            g_idx = np.asarray(g)
            if len(g_idx) <= dim + 1:
                out.append(g_idx)
                continue
            local_reduced = _umap(emb[g_idx], dim, self.local_neighbors, self.random_state)
            for local in _gmm_soft(
                local_reduced, self.threshold, self.max_clusters, self.random_state
            ):
                out.append(g_idx[np.asarray(local)])
        return out

parsed.module_docstring:
Alternative clustering strategies.

* ``gmm``: Gaussian mixture on the raw (unit-normalised) embeddings, BIC-chosen size, soft.
* ``pca_gmm``: PCA to ``reduction_dimension`` then a soft GMM (single level).
* ``agglomerative``: average-linkage cosine clustering (by distance threshold or size).
* ``hdbscan``: UMAP reduction + HDBSCAN; noise points join the nearest cluster.
* ``kmeans_silhouette``: k-means with ``k`` chosen by cosine silhouette.
* ``contiguous``: segments of *adjacent* nodes, cut where neighbours are least similar.
  This keeps narrative order, which suits stories.

Every strategy respects ``max_cluster_tokens``: an oversized cluster is re-clustered on
its own, and split in order if that makes no progress.

symbols.name: _unit_rows
symbols.text:
def _unit_rows(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    norms = np.linalg.norm(x, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    norms[norms == 0] = 1.0
    return x / norms

symbols.docstring:
Segment the (ordered) nodes into runs of adjacent nodes.

Picks ``round(n / target_size)`` segments of ``min_size``..``max_size`` nodes that
minimise the total similarity across the cut points (dynamic programming), so cuts
fall where neighbouring nodes are least alike. Clusters come back in input order, so
higher layers stay in narrative order too.
symbols.text:
class ContiguousClustering(TokenLimitedClustering):
    """Segment the (ordered) nodes into runs of adjacent nodes.

    Picks ``round(n / target_size)`` segments of ``min_size``..``max_size`` nodes that
    minimise the total similarity across the cut points (dynamic programming), so cuts
    fall where neighbouring nodes are least alike. Clusters come back in input order, so
    higher layers stay in narrative order too.
    """

symbols.name: __init__
symbols.signature: def __init__(self, target_size: int = 5, min_size: int | None = None, max_size: int | None = None, **kw: Any,) -> None
symbols.text:
def __init__(
        self,
        target_size: int = 5,
        min_size: int | None = None,
        max_size: int | None = None,
        **kw: Any,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(**kw)
        self.target_size = max(1, target_size)
        self.min_size = min_size if min_size is not None else max(1, self.target_size // 2)
        self.max_size = max_size if max_size is not None else 2 * self.target_size

symbols.name: groups
symbols.signature: def groups(self, emb: np.ndarray, tokens: np.ndarray) -> list[list[int]]
symbols.text:
def groups(self, emb: np.ndarray, tokens: np.ndarray) -> list[list[int]]:
        n = len(emb)
        if n <= self.target_size:
            return [list(range(n))]
        x = _unit_rows(emb)
        gap_sim = np.sum(x[:-1] * x[1:], axis=1)  # gap i sits between rows i and i+1
        lo, hi = min(self.min_size, n), max(self.max_size, 1)
        k = max(2, round(n / self.target_size))
        k = min(max(k, math.ceil(n / hi)), max(1, n // lo))
        cuts = self._best_cuts(gap_sim, tokens, n, k, lo, hi)
        if cuts is None:  # infeasible with the size bounds: fall back to equal runs
            size = math.ceil(n / k)
            cuts = list(range(size, n, size))
        bounds = [0, *cuts, n]
        return [list(range(a, b)) for a, b in itertools.pairwise(bounds)]

RAPTOR for codebases: symbol-level trees, code graph, hybrid search and Q&A.

>>> from raptor.code import CodeIndex
>>> index = CodeIndex.build("path/to/repo")          # doctest: +SKIP

Evaluation helpers for code retrieval: SWE-bench localization and repo QA judging.

Localization measures whether the files and functions edited by an issue's gold patch
are retrieved for the issue text (retrieval only, no reader calls). Baselines:

* ``lines``      flat line-window RAG (40-line windows, 10 lines overlap)
* ``symbols``    flat symbol-chunk RAG (leaf nodes only)
* ``structural`` symbol leaves + class / file / dir / repo summaries
* ``full``       structural + semantic concept nodes

each with or without BM25 fusion and call-graph expansion.

parsed.module_docstring:
Build the code tree: symbol leaves, structural summaries and concept nodes.

Layers (a DAG; a node may have several parents)::

    0          symbol leaves (functions, methods, class headers, module code)
    1          classes
    2          files
    3 .. 3+h   directories (by height: a directory sits above all its subdirectories)
    R          the repository
    R + 1      concepts (clusters of file and class nodes, cutting across directories)

Every summary node records ``input_hash`` (a hash of its prompt). When an index is
rebuilt or updated, a node whose prompt is unchanged reuses its previous summary and
embedding, so only the ancestors of changed code are summarized again.

        self.emb = embedding_model
        self.summ = summarization_model

        self.progress = progress or (lambda _ev: None)
        self.stats = BuildStats()
        self._nodes: list[Node] = []
        self.concept_pool: list[str] = []

def build(
        self,
        repo_name: str,
        parsed: dict[str, ParsedFile],
        sources: dict[str, str],
        readme: str | None = None,
    ) -> Tree:
        cfg = self.cfg
        paths = sorted(parsed)

        # ---- layer 0: symbol leaves
        leaves_by_file: dict[str, list[Leaf]] = {}
        for p in paths:
            leaves_by_file[p] = make_leaves(parsed[p], sources[p], self.tok, cfg.chunking)
        leaf_nodes: dict[str, list[Node]] = {}
        for p in paths:
            nodes = []
            for leaf in leaves_by_file[p]:
                meta = leaf.metadata()
                part = f"#{leaf.part[0]}" if leaf.part else ""
                meta["key"] = f"sym:{p}::{leaf.symbol}{part}@{leaf.start_line}"
                nodes.append(self._new_node(leaf.text, 0, set(), meta))
            leaf_nodes[p] = nodes
        all_leaves = [n for p in paths for n in leaf_nodes[p]]
        self._embed(all_leaves, 0)

        if cfg.summary.depth == "symbol":
            self._symbol_summaries(all_leaves, parsed)

        # ---- layer 1: classes
        class_nodes: dict[str, dict[str, Node]] = defaultdict(dict)
        class_jobs: list[tuple[str, str, list[Node]]] = []
        for p in paths:
            groups: dict[str, list[Node]] = defaultdict(list)
            for n in leaf_nodes[p]:
                if n.metadata.get("class_name"):
                    groups[n.metadata["class_name"]].append(n)
            for cls_name, members in groups.items():
                if len(members) >= 2:
                    class_jobs.append((p, cls_name, members))
        self._build_classes(class_jobs, parsed, class_nodes)

        # ---- layer 2: files
        file_nodes = self._build_files(paths, parsed, sources, leaf_nodes, class_nodes)

        # ---- layers 3+: directories, then the repo
        dir_nodes, repo_node = self._build_dirs_and_repo(repo_name, file_nodes, readme)

        # ---- concept layer
        concept_nodes = []
        if cfg.concepts.enabled:
            members = [n for p in paths for n in class_nodes[p].values()] + [
                file_nodes[p] for p in paths if p in file_nodes
            ]
            concept_nodes = self._build_concepts(members, repo_node.layer + 1)

        layer_to_nodes: dict[int, list[Node]] = defaultdict(list)
        for n in self._nodes:
            layer_to_nodes[n.layer].append(n)
        all_nodes = {n.index: n for n in self._nodes}
        top = max(layer_to_nodes)
        roots = {repo_node.index: repo_node}
        roots.update({n.index: n for n in concept_nodes})
        tree = Tree(
            all_nodes=all_nodes,
            root_nodes=roots,
            leaf_nodes={n.index: n for n in all_leaves},
            num_layers=top,
            layer_to_nodes=dict(sorted(layer_to_nodes.items())),
            metadata={
                "kind": "code",
                "repo": repo_name,
                "embedding_key": cfg.embedding_key,
                "embedding_model": self.emb.model_id,
                "summarization_model": self.summ.model_id,
                "summary_depth": cfg.summary.depth,
                "concept_pool": self.concept_pool,
                "layers": {
                    "symbol": 0,
                    "class": 1,
                    "file": 2,
                    "dir": [3, repo_node.layer - 1] if dir_nodes else None,
                    "repo": repo_node.layer,
                    "concept": repo_node.layer + 1 if concept_nodes else None,
                },
            },
        )
        tree.validate()
        self.progress(
            {"stage": "done", "num_nodes": len(tree.all_nodes), "num_layers": tree.num_layers}
        )
        return tree

def _symbol_summaries(self, leaves: list[Node], parsed: dict[str, ParsedFile]) -> None:
        targets = [
            n for n in leaves if n.metadata["symbol_kind"] in ("function", "method", "merged")
        ]
        ps = [
            self._fmt_prompt(
                prompts.SYMBOL_PROMPT,
                language=n.metadata["language"],
                symbol_kind=n.metadata["symbol_kind"],
                path=n.metadata["path"],
                code=self._truncate(n.text, self.cfg.summary.file_context_tokens),
            )
            for n in targets
        ]
        summaries = self._summarize_many(ps, 0, "symbol")
        for n, p, s in zip(targets, ps, summaries, strict=True):
            n.metadata["summary"] = s
            n.metadata["input_hash"] = short_hash(p)

symbols.text:
def _build_classes(
        self,
        jobs: list[tuple[str, str, list[Node]]],
        parsed: dict[str, ParsedFile],
        out: dict[str, dict[str, Node]],
    ) -> None:
        symbol_depth = self.cfg.summary.depth == "symbol"
        texts: list[str] = []
        metas: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        ps: list[str] = []
        for path, cls_name, members in jobs:
            sym = next((s for s in parsed[path].symbols if s.qualname == cls_name), None)
            header = next((m for m in members if m.metadata["symbol_kind"] == "class"), None)
            header_code = header.text if header else (sym.signature if sym else f"class {cls_name}")
            outline = []
            for m in members:
                if m.metadata["symbol_kind"] == "class":
                    continue
                label = m.metadata.get("signature") or m.metadata["symbol"]
                desc = (
                    m.metadata.get("summary")
                    if symbol_depth
                    else _first_line(m.metadata.get("docstring", ""))
                )
                outline.append((label, desc or ""))
            meta = {
                "kind": "class",
                "path": path,
                "symbol": cls_name,
                "start_line": sym.start_line
                if sym
                else min(m.metadata["start_line"] for m in members),
                "end_line": sym.end_line if sym else max(m.metadata["end_line"] for m in members),
                "signature": sym.signature if sym else "",
                "docstring": sym.docstring if sym else "",
                "bases": sym.bases if sym else [],
                "language": parsed[path].language,
                "key": f"class:{path}::{cls_name}",
            }
            if symbol_depth:
                members_txt = self._fit_children(outline, self.cfg.summary.group_context_tokens)
                ps.append(
                    self._fmt_prompt(
                        prompts.CLASS_PROMPT,
                        language=parsed[path].language,
                        name=cls_name,
                        path=path,
                        header=self._truncate(header_code, 800),
                        members=members_txt,
                    )
                )
            else:
                # File depth: an extractive outline (no LLM call).
                lines = [f"{meta['signature'] or 'class ' + cls_name}"]
                if meta["docstring"]:
                    lines.append(self._truncate(str(meta["docstring"]), 300))
                lines.append("Methods:")
                lines.extend(f"- {lbl}" + (f": {d}" if d else "") for lbl, d in outline)
                texts.append("\n".join(lines))
            metas.append(meta)
        if symbol_depth:
            summaries = self._summarize_many(ps, 1, "class")
            for meta, p, s in zip(metas, ps, summaries, strict=True):
                meta["summary"] = s
                meta["input_hash"] = short_hash(p)
                texts.append(s)
        nodes = []
        for (path, cls_name, members), meta, body in zip(jobs, metas, texts, strict=True):
            if not symbol_depth:
                meta["summary"] = body
            text = f"Class {cls_name} in {path}\n{body}"
            node = self._new_node(text, 1, {m.index for m in members}, meta)
            out[path][cls_name] = node
            nodes.append(node)
        self._embed(nodes, 1)

symbols.text:
def _build_files(
        self,
        paths: list[str],
        parsed: dict[str, ParsedFile],
        sources: dict[str, str],
        leaf_nodes: dict[str, list[Node]],
        class_nodes: dict[str, dict[str, Node]],
    ) -> dict[str, Node]:
        jobs: list[tuple[str, list[Node], str | None, str | None]] = []
        for p in paths:
            if not leaf_nodes[p]:
                continue
            classes = class_nodes.get(p, {})
            children: list[Node] = list(classes.values())
            children += [n for n in leaf_nodes[p] if n.metadata.get("class_name") not in classes]
            children.sort(key=lambda n: n.metadata.get("start_line", 0))
            if self._ntok(sources[p]) < TINY_FILE_TOKENS:
                jobs.append((p, children, None, sources[p].strip()))
            else:
                body = self._file_body(p, parsed[p], sources[p], children)
                jobs.append(
                    (p, children, self._fmt_prompt(prompts.FILE_PROMPT, path=p, body=body), None)
                )
        llm = [j for j in jobs if j[2] is not None]
        summaries = iter(self._summarize_many([j[2] for j in llm if j[2]], 2, "file"))
        out: dict[str, Node] = {}
        for p, children, prompt, extractive in jobs:
            summary = next(summaries) if prompt is not None else f"Small file:\n{extractive}"
            pf = parsed[p]
            meta: dict[str, Any] = {
                "kind": "file",
                "path": p,
                "symbol": p,
                "start_line": 1,
                "end_line": max(1, pf.num_lines),
                "language": pf.language,
                "summary": summary,
                "key": f"file:{p}",
            }
            if prompt is not None:
                meta["input_hash"] = short_hash(prompt)
            out[p] = self._new_node(f"File {p}\n{summary}", 2, {c.index for c in children}, meta)
        self._embed(list(out.values()), 2)
        return out

symbols.text:
def _summarize_groups(
        self,
        names: list[str],
        children_of: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
        file_nodes: dict[str, Node],
        dir_nodes: dict[str, Node],
        layer: int,
        *,
        kind: str,
        repo_name: str = "",
        readme: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        jobs: list[tuple[str, list[Node], str | None]] = []
        for d in names:
            kids = [file_nodes[n] if k == "file" else dir_nodes[n] for k, n in children_of[d]]
            kids.sort(key=lambda n: (n.metadata["kind"] != "dir", n.metadata["path"]))
            if kind == "dir" and len(kids) == 1:
                jobs.append((d, kids, None))  # a single child: reuse its summary
                continue
            items = [
                (
                    f"{'directory' if c.metadata['kind'] == 'dir' else 'file'} `{c.metadata['path']}`",
                    c.metadata.get("summary", ""),
                )
                for c in kids
            ]
            listing = self._fit_children(items, self.cfg.summary.group_context_tokens)
            if kind == "dir":
                prompt = self._fmt_prompt(prompts.DIR_PROMPT, path=d, children=listing)
            else:
                prompt = self._fmt_prompt(
                    prompts.REPO_PROMPT, name=repo_name, readme=readme, children=listing
                )
            jobs.append((d, kids, prompt))
        summaries = iter(
            self._summarize_many([p for _, _, p in jobs if p is not None], layer, kind)
        )
        new = []
        for d, kids, job_prompt in jobs:
            summary = (
                str(kids[0].metadata.get("summary", "")) if job_prompt is None else next(summaries)
            )
            meta: dict[str, Any] = {
                "kind": kind,
                "path": d if kind == "dir" else ".",
                "symbol": d if kind == "dir" else repo_name,
                "start_line": 0,
                "end_line": 0,
                "summary": summary,
                "key": f"dir:{d}" if kind == "dir" else "repo",
            }
            if job_prompt is not None:
                meta["input_hash"] = short_hash(job_prompt)
            label = f"Directory {d}/" if kind == "dir" else f"Repository {repo_name}"
            node = self._new_node(f"{label}\n{summary}", layer, {k.index for k in kids}, meta)
            dir_nodes[d] = node
            new.append(node)
        self._embed(new, layer)

symbols.name: _build_concepts
symbols.signature: def _build_concepts(self, members: list[Node], layer: int) -> list[Node]
symbols.text:
def _build_concepts(self, members: list[Node], layer: int) -> list[Node]:
        cc = self.cfg.concepts
        if len(members) < cc.min_nodes:
            return []
        key = self.cfg.embedding_key
        by_key = {m.metadata["key"]: i for i, m in enumerate(members)}
        self.concept_pool = sorted(by_key)
        emb = np.stack([np.asarray(m.embeddings[key], np.float32) for m in members])
        clusters: list[list[int]]
        if self.reuse.concepts:
            clusters = self._reuse_concepts(by_key, emb)
        else:
            self.progress({"stage": "clustering", "layer": layer, "total": len(members)})
            tokens = [self._ntok(m.metadata.get("summary", m.text)) for m in members]
            clusterer = make_clusterer(cc.clustering)
            clusters = clusterer.cluster(emb, tokens)
        clusters = [c for c in clusters if len(c) >= cc.min_members and len(c) < len(members)]
        if not clusters:
            return []
        ps = []
        for c in clusters:
            group = sorted((members[i] for i in c), key=lambda n: n.metadata["key"])
            items = [
                (
                    f"{g.metadata['kind']} `{g.metadata['path']}"
                    + (f"::{g.metadata['symbol']}`" if g.metadata["kind"] == "class" else "`"),
                    g.metadata.get("summary", ""),
                )
                for g in group
            ]
            ps.append(
                self._fmt_prompt(
                    prompts.CONCEPT_PROMPT,
                    children=self._fit_children(items, self.cfg.summary.group_context_tokens),
                )
            )
        summaries = self._summarize_many(ps, layer, "concept")
        nodes = []
        for i, (c, p, s) in enumerate(zip(clusters, ps, summaries, strict=True)):
            name = _concept_name(s) or f"concept {i + 1}"
            paths = sorted({members[j].metadata["path"] for j in c})
            meta = {
                "kind": "concept",
                "path": paths[0] if len(paths) == 1 else posixpath.commonpath(paths) or ".",
                "paths": paths,
                "symbol": name,
                "start_line": 0,
                "end_line": 0,
                "summary": s,
                "input_hash": short_hash(p),
                "key": f"concept:{i}",
            }
            nodes.append(
                self._new_node(f"Concept: {name}\n{s}", layer, {members[j].index for j in c}, meta)
            )
        self._embed(nodes, layer)
        return nodes

def _units(parsed: ParsedFile, lines: list[str]) -> list[Leaf]:
    units: list[Leaf] = []
    for sym in parsed.symbols:
        cls = top_class(sym)
        if sym.kind == "class":
            end = sym.header_end_line or sym.start_line
            code = sym.text or "\n".join(lines[sym.start_line - 1 : end])
            units.append(
                Leaf(
                    parsed.path,
                    sym.start_line,
                    max(sym.start_line, end),
                    sym.qualname,
                    "class",
                    code,
                    language=parsed.language,
                    signature=sym.signature,
                    docstring=sym.docstring,
                    decorators=sym.decorators,
                    class_name=cls,
                    symbols=[sym.qualname],
                )
            )
        else:
            units.append(
                Leaf(
                    parsed.path,
                    sym.start_line,
                    sym.end_line,
                    sym.qualname,
                    sym.kind,
                    sym.text,
                    language=parsed.language,
                    signature=sym.signature,
                    docstring=sym.docstring,
                    decorators=sym.decorators,
                    class_name=cls,
                    symbols=[sym.qualname],
                )
            )
    for a, b in parsed.module_code:
        units.append(
            Leaf(
                parsed.path,
                a,
                b,
                "<module>",
                "module",
                "\n".join(lines[a - 1 : b]),
                language=parsed.language,
                docstring=parsed.module_docstring if a == 1 else "",
                symbols=["<module>"],
            )
        )
    units.sort(key=lambda u: (u.start_line, u.end_line))
    return units

symbols.text:
def _split(unit: Leaf, tok: tiktoken.Encoding, max_tokens: int) -> list[Leaf]:
    if _ntok(tok, unit.code) <= max_tokens:
        return [unit]
    code_lines = unit.code.split("\n")
    parts: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # [start, end) indices into code_lines
    start, used = 0, 0
    for i, line in enumerate(code_lines):
        n = _ntok(tok, line) + 1
        if used + n > max_tokens and i > start:
            parts.append((start, i))
            start, used = i, 0
        used += n
    parts.append((start, len(code_lines)))
    out = []
    for k, (a, b) in enumerate(parts):
        out.append(
            Leaf(
                unit.path,
                unit.start_line + a,
                unit.start_line + b - 1,
                unit.symbol,
                unit.symbol_kind,
                "\n".join(code_lines[a:b]),
                language=unit.language,
                signature=unit.signature,
                docstring=unit.docstring if k == 0 else "",
                decorators=unit.decorators,
                class_name=unit.class_name,
                symbols=list(unit.symbols),
                part=(k + 1, len(parts)),
            )
        )
    return out

symbols.text:
def _merge(units: list[Leaf], tok: tiktoken.Encoding, cfg: ChunkConfig) -> list[Leaf]:
    """Merge runs of adjacent tiny units that share a class (or are all module level)."""
    if cfg.min_symbol_tokens <= 0:
        return units
    out: list[Leaf] = []
    run: list[Leaf] = []
    run_tokens = 0

    def flush() -> None:
        nonlocal run, run_tokens
        if not run:
            return
        if len(run) == 1:
            out.append(run[0])
        else:
            names = [s for u in run for s in u.symbols]
            out.append(
                Leaf(
                    run[0].path,
                    run[0].start_line,
                    run[-1].end_line,
                    ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(names)),
                    "merged",
                    "\n\n".join(u.code for u in run),
                    language=run[0].language,
                    signature="; ".join(u.signature for u in run if u.signature),
                    docstring="\n".join(u.docstring for u in run if u.docstring),
                    class_name=run[0].class_name,
                    symbols=list(dict.fromkeys(names)),
                )
            )
        run, run_tokens = [], 0

    for u in units:
        n = _ntok(tok, u.code)
        tiny = n < cfg.min_symbol_tokens and u.part is None
        if not tiny:
            flush()
            out.append(u)
            continue
        if run and (run[-1].class_name != u.class_name or run_tokens + n > cfg.max_symbol_tokens):
            flush()
        run.append(u)
        run_tokens += n
        if run_tokens >= cfg.min_symbol_tokens:
            flush()
    flush()
    return out

symbols.text:
@code_app.command("index")
def index_cmd(
    path: Annotated[
        Path, typer.Argument(help="Repository to index.", exists=True, file_okay=False)
    ],
    out: Annotated[Path, typer.Option("--out", "-o", help="Directory to write the index to.")],
    summary_depth: Annotated[
        str,
        typer.Option("--summary-depth", help="symbol: summarize every symbol; file: files only."),
    ] = "file",
    config: Annotated[Path | None, typer.Option("--config", "-c", help="YAML CodeConfig.")] = None,
    concepts: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="Build the semantic concept layer.")] = True,
    exclude: Annotated[
        list[str] | None,
        typer.Option("--exclude", "-x", help="Extra gitignore-style pattern to skip."),
    ] = None,
    summary_provider: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option(help="Summaries via 'gemini' or 'ollama' (default: models.provider)."),
    ] = None,
    overwrite: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="Replace an existing index at --out.")] = False,
    verbose: VerboseOpt = False,
) -> None:
    """Build a code index for a repository."""
    _setup_logging(verbose)
    from .config import CodeConfig
    from .index import CodeIndex

    if summary_depth not in ("symbol", "file"):
        raise typer.BadParameter("--summary-depth must be 'symbol' or 'file'")
    if (out / "code.json").exists() and not overwrite:
        raise typer.BadParameter(f"{out} already holds an index; pass --overwrite or use `update`")
    cfg = CodeConfig.from_yaml(config) if config else CodeConfig()
    cfg.summary.depth = summary_depth  # type: ignore[assignment]
    cfg.concepts.enabled = concepts
    if exclude:
        cfg.ingest.exclude = [*cfg.ingest.exclude, *exclude]
    if summary_provider:
        cfg.models.summary_provider = summary_provider  # type: ignore[assignment]
    idx = CodeIndex.build(path, cfg, progress=_progress)
    idx.save(out)
    st = idx.stats()
    typer.echo(
        f"Indexed {st['files']} files -> {sum(st['nodes'].values())} nodes {st['nodes']}, "
        f"edges {st['edges']} -> {out}"
    )
    typer.echo(f"Model calls: {idx.last_build_stats}")

@code_app.command()
def search(
    index: IndexDir,
    query: Annotated[str, typer.Argument()],
    k: Annotated[int, typer.Option("--top-k", "-k")] = 10,
    bm25: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="Use BM25 over identifiers.")] = True,
    dense: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="Use dense embeddings.")] = True,
    graph: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="Expand hits along the call graph.")] = True,
    as_json: JsonOpt = False,
    verbose: VerboseOpt = False,
) -> None:
    """Search the index (hybrid BM25 + dense, with graph expansion)."""
    _setup_logging(verbose)
    idx = _load(index)
    hits = idx.search(query, k, bm25=bm25, dense=dense, graph_expansion=graph)
    if as_json:
        typer.echo(json.dumps([h.to_dict() for h in hits], indent=2))
        return
    for i, h in enumerate(hits, 1):
        first = next((ln for ln in h.text.splitlines() if ln.strip()), "")
        typer.echo(f"{i:2d}. [{h.kind:7s}] {h.location}  {h.symbol}  ({h.score:.4f})")
        typer.echo(f"      {first[:110]}")

symbols.text:
@code_app.command()
def tree(
    index: IndexDir,
    depth: Annotated[int, typer.Option(help="Levels to print below the repo.")] = 3,
    summaries: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="Show the first line of each summary.")] = False,
) -> None:
    """Print the structural hierarchy (repo > dirs > files > classes > symbols) and concepts."""
    idx = _load(index)
    st = idx.stats()
    typer.echo(f"{st['repo_path']}: {st['files']} files, nodes {st['nodes']}, edges {st['edges']}")
    for d, h in idx.outline(max_depth=depth):
        label = {
            "repo": f"{h.symbol}/",
            "dir": f"{h.path}/",
            "file": h.path,
            "class": f"class {h.symbol}  :{h.start_line}-{h.end_line}",
            "symbol": f"{h.symbol}  :{h.start_line}-{h.end_line}",
            "concept": f"[concept] {h.symbol}",
        }.get(h.kind, h.symbol)
        line = "  " * d + label
        if summaries and h.kind != "symbol":
            body = h.text.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in h.text else h.text
            first = next((ln for ln in body.splitlines() if ln.strip()), "")
            line += f"  — {first[:100]}"
        typer.echo(line)

parsed.module_docstring:
Best-effort static code graph: imports, calls and inheritance.

Edges are computed between *symbol keys* ``(path, qualname)``; a ``qualname`` of ``None``
means the file itself. :class:`raptor.code.index.CodeIndex` maps the keys to tree nodes.

Resolution is purely syntactic and deliberately conservative: a call is linked only
when it resolves through ``self``/``super()``, an import binding, the same file, or a
repo-wide *unique* name. Dynamic dispatch and duck typing are not followed.

@classmethod
    def build(
        cls,
        repo_path: str | Path,
        config: CodeConfig | None = None,
        *,
        embedding_model: BaseEmbeddingModel | None = None,
        summarization_model: BaseSummarizationModel | None = None,
        qa_model: BaseQAModel | None = None,
        progress: ProgressCallback | None = None,
    ) -> CodeIndex:
        """Parse, summarize and embed the repository at ``repo_path``."""
        config = config or CodeConfig()
        root = Path(repo_path).resolve()
        if not root.is_dir():
            raise NotADirectoryError(f"{root} is not a directory")
        models = LazyModels(
            config.models,
            embedding=embedding_model,
            summarization=summarization_model,
            qa=qa_model,
        )
        index = cls(root, config, Tree.from_layers({0: []}), [], {}, models=models)
        index._rebuild(progress or _noop, previous=None)
        return index

def _rebuild(
        self,
        progress: ProgressCallback,
        *,
        previous: CodeIndex | None,
    ) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, int]]:
        prev_files = previous._files if previous is not None else None
        parsed, sources, records, changed = self._scan(progress, prev_files)
        if not parsed:
            raise ValueError(f"no indexable source files found under {self.repo_path}")
        reuse = (
            Reuse.from_tree(previous.tree, self.models.embedding.model_id)
            if previous is not None
            else Reuse()
        )
        builder = CodeTreeBuilder(
            self.config,
            self.models.embedding,
            self.models.summarization,
            self.tokenizer,
            reuse=reuse,
            progress=progress,
        )
        tree = builder.build(self.repo_path.name, parsed, sources, self._readme())
        self.tree = tree
        self._files = records
        self.edges = self._compute_edges(parsed)
        self.git_commit = git_head(self.repo_path)
        self.dirty = (
            sorted(git_changed_files(self.repo_path, self.git_commit) or set())
            if (self.git_commit)
            else []
        )
        self._searcher = None
        stats = {
            "reembedded": builder.stats.reembedded,
            "resummarized": builder.stats.resummarized,
            "reused_summaries": builder.stats.reused_summaries,
            "reused_embeddings": builder.stats.reused_embeddings,
        }
        self.last_build_stats = stats
        return changed, stats

symbols.docstring:
Re-index what changed since the last build/update.

Changed files are found with ``git diff`` against the indexed commit when the repo
is a git checkout (confirmed by content hash), otherwise by hashing every file.
Only changed symbols are re-embedded and only their ancestors are re-summarized.
symbols.text:
def update(self, progress: ProgressCallback | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Re-index what changed since the last build/update.

        Changed files are found with ``git diff`` against the indexed commit when the repo
        is a git checkout (confirmed by content hash), otherwise by hashing every file.
        Only changed symbols are re-embedded and only their ancestors are re-summarized.
        """
        progress = progress or _noop
        candidates: set[str] | None = None
        if self.git_commit and git_head(self.repo_path) is not None:
            diff = git_changed_files(self.repo_path, self.git_commit)
            if diff is not None:
                candidates = diff | set(self.dirty)
        old_files = dict(self._files)
        current = set(discover_files(self.repo_path, self.config.ingest, self._extractors().keys()))
        added = current - old_files.keys()
        deleted = old_files.keys() - current
        to_check = (candidates & current) | added if candidates is not None else current
        changed: list[str] = []
        for rel in sorted(to_check):
            data = read_source(self.repo_path, rel, self.config.ingest)
            sha = sha256_bytes(data) if data is not None else None
            if sha is None or rel not in old_files or old_files[rel]["sha"] != sha:
                changed.append(rel)
        changed_all = sorted(set(changed) | deleted)
        if not changed_all:
            return {"changed_files": [], "reembedded": 0, "resummarized": 0}
        previous = CodeIndex(
            self.repo_path,
            self.config,
            self.tree,
            self.edges,
            old_files,
            models=self.models,
            git_commit=self.git_commit,
        )
        # Files with an unchanged hash reuse their stored parse; only changed ones are parsed.
        _, stats = self._rebuild(progress, previous=previous)
        return {
            "changed_files": changed_all,
            "reembedded": stats["reembedded"],
            "resummarized": stats["resummarized"],
        }

def save(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
        path = Path(path)
        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_tree(self.tree, path / TREE_DIR)
        _write_json(
            path / CODE_FILE,
            {
                "format_version": FORMAT_VERSION,
                "repo_path": str(self.repo_path),
                "config": self.config.model_dump(mode="json"),
                "git_commit": self.git_commit,
                "dirty": self.dirty,
                "saved_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                "files": self._files,
            },
        )
        _write_json(path / GRAPH_FILE, {"edges": [e.to_dict() for e in self.edges]})
        return path

        summarization_model: BaseSummarizationModel | None = None,
        qa_model: BaseQAModel | None = None,
    ) -> CodeIndex:
        path = Path(path)
        code_file = path / CODE_FILE
        if not code_file.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no code index at {path} (missing {CODE_FILE})")
        doc = json.loads(code_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if doc.get("format_version") != FORMAT_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported code index format {doc.get('format_version')!r}")
        cfg = config or CodeConfig.model_validate(doc["config"])
        tree = load_tree(path / TREE_DIR)
        graph = json.loads((path / GRAPH_FILE).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        edges = [CodeEdge(int(e["src"]), int(e["dst"]), str(e["kind"])) for e in graph["edges"]]
        models = LazyModels(
            cfg.models,
            embedding=embedding_model,
            summarization=summarization_model,
            qa=qa_model,
        )
        return cls(
            repo_path or doc["repo_path"],
            cfg,
            tree,
            edges,
            doc["files"],
            models=models,
            git_commit=doc.get("git_commit"),
            dirty=doc.get("dirty", []),
        )

def _context(self, hits: list[CodeHit]) -> tuple[str, list[CodeHit]]:
        budget = self.config.retrieval.max_context_tokens
        parts: list[str] = []
        used: list[CodeHit] = []
        total = 0
        for h in hits:
            block = f"[{h.location}] ({h.kind} {h.symbol})\n{h.text.strip()}\n"
            n = len(self.tokenizer.encode(block, disallowed_special=()))
            if total + n > budget:
                if used:
                    continue
                block = self.tokenizer.decode(
                    self.tokenizer.encode(block, disallowed_special=())[:budget]
                )
                n = budget
            parts.append(block)
            used.append(h)
            total += n
        return CODE_QA_INSTRUCTIONS + "\n\n" + "\n".join(parts), used

def find_symbol(self, name: str) -> list[CodeHit]:
        """Nodes whose symbol, qualified name or path matches ``name`` exactly (or by suffix)."""
        name = name.strip()
        out = []
        for n in sorted(self.tree.all_nodes.values(), key=lambda n: (n.layer, n.index)):
            m = n.metadata
            names = [str(m.get("symbol", "")), *m.get("symbols", [])]
            path = str(m.get("path", ""))
            if (
                name in names
                or any(x.endswith("." + name) for x in names)
                or (
                    node_kind(n) in ("file", "dir")
                    and (path == name or path.rstrip("/") == name.rstrip("/"))
                )
            ):
                out.append(self.node_hit(n.index))
        return out

def discover_files(root: str | Path, cfg: IngestConfig, extensions: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Relative POSIX paths of the indexable source files under ``root``."""
    root = Path(root)
    exts = tuple(e.lower() for e in extensions)
    candidates = (_git_files(root) if cfg.use_git else None) or _walk_files(root)
    exclude = _pathspec(cfg.exclude) if cfg.exclude else None
    include = _pathspec(cfg.include) if cfg.include else None
    out = []
    for rel in candidates:
        if not rel.lower().endswith(exts) or _skip_by_dir(rel) or rel.endswith(GENERATED_SUFFIXES):
            continue
        if exclude is not None and exclude.match_file(rel):
            continue
        if include is not None and not include.match_file(rel):
            continue
        out.append(rel)
    return out

Files changed since commit ``since`` (committed, staged, unstaged or untracked).

Returns ``None`` when git is unavailable, so the caller falls back to hashing.
symbols.text:
def git_changed_files(root: str | Path, since: str) -> set[str] | None:
    """Files changed since commit ``since`` (committed, staged, unstaged or untracked).

    Returns ``None`` when git is unavailable, so the caller falls back to hashing.
    """
    git = shutil.which("git")
    if git is None or not (Path(root) / ".git").exists():
        return None
    changed: set[str] = set()
    try:
        diff = subprocess.run(
            [git, "-C", str(root), "diff", "--name-only", "-z", since],
            capture_output=True,
            check=True,
            timeout=60,
        ).stdout
        others = subprocess.run(
            [git, "-C", str(root), "ls-files", "-z", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
            capture_output=True,
            check=True,
            timeout=60,
        ).stdout
    except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError):
        return None
    for blob in (diff, others):
        changed.update(p for p in blob.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").split("\0") if p)
    return changed

parsed.module_docstring:
Per-language symbol extraction interface.

An extractor turns one source file into a :class:`ParsedFile`: the imports, the symbols
(functions, methods, classes) with their line spans, signatures and docstrings, and the
raw references each symbol makes (calls, base classes). Name resolution across files
happens later in :mod:`raptor.code.graph`, so extractors stay purely syntactic.

Add a language by subclassing :class:`LanguageExtractor` and registering it::

    @EXTRACTORS.register("go")
    class GoExtractor(LanguageExtractor):
        name = "go"
        extensions = (".go",)
        def parse(self, source: bytes, path: str) -> ParsedFile: ...

def _unwrap(node: Any) -> tuple[Any, list[str], Any]:
    """Return ``(definition, decorators, outer_node)`` for a possibly decorated definition."""
    if node.type == "decorated_definition":
        decorators = [_text(c).lstrip("@").strip() for c in node.children if c.type == "decorator"]
        definition = node.child_by_field_name("definition")
        return definition, decorators, node
    return node, [], node

def _signature(definition: Any, source: bytes) -> str:
    body = definition.child_by_field_name("body")
    end = body.start_byte if body is not None else definition.end_byte
    sig = source[definition.start_byte : end].decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
    sig = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", sig).rstrip(":").strip()
    sig = sig.replace("( ", "(").replace(" )", ")").replace(", )", ")")
    return sig

def _function(
        self,
        definition: Any,
        decorators: list[str],
        outer: Any,
        source: bytes,
        lines: list[str],
        *,
        parent: str | None,

            qualname=f"{parent}.{name}" if parent else name,

            signature=_signature(definition, source),
            docstring=_docstring(definition.child_by_field_name("body")),
            decorators=decorators,
            parent=parent,
            text="\n".join(lines[start - 1 : end]),

symbols.text:
def _class(
        self,
        definition: Any,
        decorators: list[str],
        outer: Any,
        source: bytes,
        lines: list[str],
        *,
        prefix: str,
    ) -> list[Symbol]:
        name_node = definition.child_by_field_name("name")
        name = _text(name_node) if name_node is not None else "<anonymous>"
        qualname = f"{prefix}{name}"
        body = definition.child_by_field_name("body")
        bases: list[str] = []
        supers = definition.child_by_field_name("superclasses")
        if supers is not None:
            for arg in supers.named_children:
                if arg.type in ("identifier", "attribute"):
                    bases.append(re.sub(r"\s+", "", _text(arg)))

        start, end = _line(outer), _end_line(outer)
        members: list[Symbol] = []
        header_lines: list[int] = list(range(start, (_line(body) if body is not None else end)))
        calls: list[str] = []
        first_member_line: int | None = None
        if body is not None:
            for child in body.named_children:
                inner, decs, inner_outer = _unwrap(child)
                if inner is not None and inner.type == "function_definition":
                    members.append(
                        self._function(inner, decs, inner_outer, source, lines, parent=qualname)
                    )
                    first_member_line = first_member_line or _line(inner_outer)
                elif inner is not None and inner.type == "class_definition":
                    members.extend(
                        self._class(inner, decs, inner_outer, source, lines, prefix=f"{qualname}.")
                    )
                    first_member_line = first_member_line or _line(inner_outer)
                else:
                    header_lines.extend(range(_line(child), _end_line(child) + 1))
                    _collect_calls(child, calls, skip_defs=True)
        header_lines = sorted(set(header_lines))
        header_text = "\n".join(lines[i - 1] for i in header_lines if 0 < i <= len(lines))
        # The header leaf's span runs up to the first method (or the whole class).
        header_end = first_member_line - 1 if first_member_line is not None else end
        while header_end > start and not lines[header_end - 1].strip():
            header_end -= 1
        cls = Symbol(
            qualname=qualname,
            name=name,
            kind="class",
            start_line=start,
            end_line=end,
            signature=_signature(definition, source),
            docstring=_docstring(body),
            decorators=decorators,
            parent=prefix.rstrip(".") or None,
            text=header_text,
            calls=_dedupe(calls),
            bases=bases,
            header_end_line=header_end,
        )
        return [cls, *members]

symbols.docstring: Tokens indexed for ``node``: identifiers (boosted), path, docstring and text.
symbols.text:
def bm25_document(node: Node) -> list[str]:
    """Tokens indexed for ``node``: identifiers (boosted), path, docstring and text."""
    m = node.metadata
    kind = node_kind(node)
    toks: list[str] = []
    names = " ".join([str(m.get("symbol", "")), *m.get("symbols", [])])
    toks += tokenize(names) * 3
    toks += tokenize(str(m.get("path", "")).replace("/", " ").replace(".py", "")) * 2
    toks += tokenize(str(m.get("signature", "")))
    toks += tokenize(str(m.get("docstring", ""))) * 2
    if kind == "symbol":
        toks += tokenize(node.text)
        if m.get("summary"):
            toks += tokenize(m["summary"])
    else:
        toks += tokenize(str(m.get("summary") or node.text))
    return toks

def dense_scores(self, query: str) -> np.ndarray:
        assert self.embedding_model is not None
        q = np.asarray(self.embedding_model.embed_query(query[:MAX_QUERY_CHARS]), np.float32)

        _, matrix = self.tree.normalized_matrix()

def _neighbors(self, idx: int, sim_of, allowed: set[int]) -> list[int]:
        nb = self.neighbors(idx)
        cands = [
            i
            for i in nb["parent_class"] + nb["callees"] + nb["callers"] + nb["bases"]
            if i in allowed and i != idx
        ]
        cands = list(dict.fromkeys(cands))
        cands.sort(key=lambda i: (-sim_of(i), i))
        return cands[: self.cfg.expansion_per_hit]

@app.command()
def run(
    configs: Annotated[list[Path], typer.Argument(help="Experiment YAML files.", exists=True)],
    runs: RootOpt = DEFAULT_RUNS_DIR,
    trees: Annotated[
        Path, typer.Option("--trees", help="Tree cache directory.")
    ] = DEFAULT_TREES_DIR,
    force: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option(help="Redo finished runs (all calls come from cache).")
    ] = False,
    workers: Annotated[int, typer.Option(help="Questions answered in parallel.")] = 4,
    verbose: Annotated[bool, typer.Option("--verbose", "-v")] = False,
) -> None:
    """Run experiment configs (skips finished ones; resumes interrupted ones)."""
    _logging(verbose)
    from .runner import Runner

    runner = Runner(runs, trees, question_workers=workers)
    outcomes = runner.run_many(sorted(configs), force=force)
    for o in outcomes:
        acc = f"{o.summary['accuracy']:.3f}" if o.summary else "-"
        cost = o.session_cost
        typer.echo(
            f"{o.status:8s} {o.run_id:48s} acc={acc}  "
            f"llm={cost.get('llm_calls', 0)} emb={cost.get('embed_calls', 0)} "
            f"hits={cost.get('cache_hits', 0)} misses={cost.get('cache_misses', 0)}"
        )
    if any(o.status == "quota" for o in outcomes):
        raise typer.Exit(code=2)

Compare two runs question by question (only questions both answered).

``fixed`` are questions ``b`` gets right and ``a`` gets wrong; ``broken`` the reverse.
symbols.text:
def paired_comparison(a: dict[str, bool], b: dict[str, bool]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare two runs question by question (only questions both answered).

    ``fixed`` are questions ``b`` gets right and ``a`` gets wrong; ``broken`` the reverse.
    """
    common = sorted(set(a) & set(b))
    fixed = [q for q in common if b[q] and not a[q]]
    broken = [q for q in common if a[q] and not b[q]]
    both_right = sum(1 for q in common if a[q] and b[q])
    both_wrong = sum(1 for q in common if not a[q] and not b[q])
    av = [a[q] for q in common]
    bv = [b[q] for q in common]
    delta = (accuracy(bv) - accuracy(av)) if common else float("nan")
    return {
        "n": len(common),
        "delta": delta,
        "delta_ci95": list(paired_bootstrap_ci(av, bv)),
        "mcnemar_p": mcnemar_exact(len(fixed), len(broken)),
        "fixed": fixed,
        "broken": broken,
        "both_right": both_right,
        "both_wrong": both_wrong,
    }

def summarize_results(rows: Sequence[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Accuracy block of ``summary.json`` from ``results.jsonl`` rows."""
    correct = [bool(r["correct"]) for r in rows]
    hard = [bool(r["correct"]) for r in rows if r.get("difficult")]
    lat = [float(r.get("latency_s", 0.0)) for r in rows]
    return {
        "n_questions": len(rows),
        "accuracy": accuracy(correct),
        "accuracy_hard": accuracy(hard) if hard else None,
        "n_hard": len(hard),
        "ci95": list(bootstrap_ci(correct)),
        "layer_share": layer_share(r.get("retrieved", []) for r in rows),
        "query_seconds_mean": float(np.mean(lat)) if lat else 0.0,
        "context_tokens_mean": float(np.mean([r.get("context_tokens", 0) for r in rows]))
        if rows
        else 0.0,
    }

def stage_rows(runs: list[dict[str, Any]], root: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Each run of a stage with its paired comparison to its baseline."""
    out = []
    for run in _order(runs):
        base = _baseline_for(run, runs) or _baseline_for(run, list_runs(root))
        cmp = compare_runs(base["run_id"], run["run_id"], root) if base else None
        out.append({"run": run, "base": base, "cmp": cmp, "verdict": _verdict(cmp)})
    return out

def _table(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    head = (
        "| Run | Varies | Setting | vs | Acc % | 95% CI | Hard acc % | Δ vs base (pts) [95% CI] "
        "| McNemar p | fixed / broken | Summary-node share % | LLM calls | Build s/story "
        "| Nodes/tree | Verdict |\n"
        "|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|\n"
    )
    lines = []
    for row in rows:
        r, cmp = row["run"], row["cmp"]
        lo, hi = r["ci95"]
        if cmp:
            dlo, dhi = cmp["delta_ci95"]
            delta = f"{100 * cmp['delta']:+.1f} [{100 * dlo:+.1f}, {100 * dhi:+.1f}]"
            p = f"{cmp['mcnemar_p']:.3f}"
            fb = f"{len(cmp['fixed'])} / {len(cmp['broken'])}"
        else:
            delta, p, fb = "-", "-", "-"
        lines.append(
            f"| `{r['name']}` | {r.get('factor') or '-'} | {_setting(r)} "
            f"| {('`' + row['base']['name'] + '`') if row['base'] else '-'} | {_pct(r['accuracy'])} "
            f"| {_pct(lo)}–{_pct(hi)} | {_pct(r.get('accuracy_hard'))} | {delta} | {p} | {fb} "
            f"| {_pct(_summary_share(r), 0)} | {r['cost'].get('llm_calls', 0)} "
            f"| {r.get('build_seconds', 0):.0f} | {r['tree_stats'].get('mean_nodes', 0):.0f} "
            f"| {row['verdict']} |"
        )
    return head + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def _forest(rows: list[dict[str, Any]], path: Path, title: str) -> None:
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    n = len(rows)
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(
        1, 2, figsize=(11, 0.42 * n + 1.6), sharey=True, gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1]}
    )
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    labels = [r["run"]["name"] for r in rows]
    ys = list(range(n))[::-1]
    for y, row in zip(ys, rows, strict=True):
        r = row["run"]
        lo, hi = r["ci95"]
        is_base = row["cmp"] is None
        color = INK_2 if is_base else SERIES[0]
        ax1.plot([100 * lo, 100 * hi], [y, y], color=color, linewidth=2, solid_capstyle="round")
        ax1.plot(100 * r["accuracy"], y, "o", color=color, markersize=8, markeredgecolor=SURFACE)
        if row["cmp"]:
            c = row["cmp"]
            dlo, dhi = c["delta_ci95"]
            sig = c["mcnemar_p"] < ALPHA
            dcol = (SERIES[2] if c["delta"] > 0 else SERIES[1]) if sig else SERIES[0]
            ax2.plot(
                [100 * dlo, 100 * dhi], [y, y], color=dcol, linewidth=2, solid_capstyle="round"
            )
            ax2.plot(100 * c["delta"], y, "o", color=dcol, markersize=8, markeredgecolor=SURFACE)
    bases = {row["run"]["run_id"]: row["run"]["accuracy"] for row in rows if row["cmp"] is None}
    bases.update({row["base"]["run_id"]: row["base"]["accuracy"] for row in rows if row["base"]})
    for b in bases.values():
        ax1.axvline(100 * b, color=INK_2, linewidth=1, linestyle=(0, (3, 3)))
    ax2.axvline(0, color=INK_2, linewidth=1)
    ax1.set_yticks(ys, labels, color=INK, fontsize=9)
    ax1.set_xlabel("Accuracy % (95% bootstrap CI)", color=INK_2, fontsize=9)
    ax2.set_xlabel("Δ vs baseline, points (paired 95% CI)", color=INK_2, fontsize=9)
    for ax in (ax1, ax2):
        _style(ax)
    fig.suptitle(title, color=INK, fontsize=11, x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.text(
        0.01,
        0.005,
        "Grey = baseline; dashed lines = baseline accuracies. Right panel: green/orange = McNemar p < 0.05 better/worse; blue = within noise.",
        color=INK_2,
        fontsize=8,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.03, 1, 0.97))
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=130, facecolor=SURFACE)
    plt.close(fig)

def _layer_share(runs: list[dict[str, Any]], path: Path) -> None:
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    runs = [r for r in runs if r.get("method") == "raptor"]
    if not runs:
        return
    layers = sorted({int(k) for r in runs for k in r.get("layer_share", {})})
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 0.36 * len(runs) + 1.4))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ys = list(range(len(runs)))[::-1]
    left = [0.0] * len(runs)
    for li, layer in enumerate(layers):
        vals = [100 * r.get("layer_share", {}).get(str(layer), 0.0) for r in runs]
        label = "leaves (layer 0)" if layer == 0 else f"layer {layer} summaries"
        ax.barh(
            ys,
            vals,
            left=left,
            height=0.62,
            color=SERIES[min(li, len(SERIES) - 1)],
            edgecolor=SURFACE,
            linewidth=2,
            label=label,
        )
        left = [a + b for a, b in zip(left, vals, strict=True)]
    ax.set_yticks(ys, [f"{r['name']} ({r['split']})" for r in runs], color=INK, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
    ax.set_xlabel("Share of retrieved nodes, %", color=INK_2, fontsize=9)
    _style(ax)
    ax.legend(
        loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0), ncol=len(layers), frameon=False, fontsize=8
    )
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=130, facecolor=SURFACE)
    plt.close(fig)

symbols.text:
def generate_report(
    root: str | Path = DEFAULT_RUNS_DIR,
    out_dir: str | Path = DEFAULT_OUT_DIR,
    *,
    title: str = "RAPTOR strategy sweep on QuALITY",
    figures: bool = True,
) -> Path:
    root, out_dir = Path(root), Path(out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fig_dir = out_dir / "figures"
    runs = list_runs(root)
    stages: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for r in runs:
        stages.setdefault(r.get("stage") or "other", []).append(r)

    parts = [f"# {title}\n"]
    parts.append(
        f"_Generated {datetime.now(timezone.utc):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC by `raptor eval report` from "
        f"{len(runs)} runs in `{root.as_posix()}`. Do not edit by hand: conclusions live in "
        "`conclusions.md`._\n"
    )
    splits = sorted({(r["split"], r["n_questions"], r.get("n_stories", 0)) for r in runs})
    if splits:
        desc = ", ".join(f"`{s}` = {n} questions over {k} stories" for s, n, k in splits)
        readers = sorted({r.get("reader_model", "?") for r in runs})
        parts.append(
            "## Setup\n\n"
            f"- Splits (`configs/splits.yaml`): {desc}. Dev and confirm use disjoint articles.\n"
            f"- Reader (fixed): {', '.join(f'`{m}`' for m in readers)} with JSON-mode MCQ answers.\n"
            "- Accuracy CIs: percentile bootstrap (10k resamples). Δ CIs: paired bootstrap over "
            "questions. p-values: exact two-sided McNemar test on the discordant pairs vs the "
            "run's baseline.\n"
            "- **Noise floor:** with ~70 questions a 95% CI on accuracy is about ±11 points, so "
            'only large, consistent differences mean anything. "Within noise" below means '
            f"McNemar p ≥ {ALPHA}.\n"
            '- "Summary-node share" is the fraction of retrieved nodes that are summaries '
            "(layer ≥ 1) rather than leaf chunks. LLM calls count summaries + answers that were "
            "not already cached when the run happened.\n"
        )
    conclusions = out_dir / "conclusions.md"
    if conclusions.exists():
        parts.append(conclusions.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() + "\n")

    for stage in sorted(stages):
        rows = stage_rows(stages[stage], root)
        label = {
            "A": "Stage A: one factor at a time (dev)",
            "B": "Stage B: combinations (dev)",
            "C": "Stage C: held-out confirm set",
        }.get(stage, f"Stage {stage}")
        parts.append(f"## {label}\n")
        if figures and rows:
            fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            fname = f"stage_{stage.lower()}.png"
            _forest(rows, fig_dir / fname, label)
            parts.append(f"![{label}](figures/{fname})\n")
        parts.append(_table(rows))
        noisy = [r["run"]["name"] for r in rows if r["verdict"] == "within noise"]
        sig = [
            f"`{r['run']['name']}` ({r['verdict'].strip('*')})"
            for r in rows
            if r["verdict"].startswith("**")
        ]
        parts.append(
            f"\nSignificant vs baseline: {', '.join(sig) if sig else 'none'}. "
            f"Within noise: {len(noisy)} of {sum(1 for r in rows if r['cmp'])} comparisons.\n"
        )

    if figures and runs:
        fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _layer_share(runs, fig_dir / "layer_share.png")
        parts.append(
            "## Where retrieved context comes from\n\n![Layer share](figures/layer_share.png)\n"
        )

    if runs:
        total = {
            k: sum(r["cost"].get(k, 0) for r in runs)
            for k in ("llm_calls", "embed_calls", "cache_hits", "cache_misses")
        }
        parts.append(
            "## Cost\n\n"
            f"Across all runs: {total['llm_calls']} LLM calls, {total['embed_calls']} embedded "
            f"texts (local + API), {total['cache_hits']} cache hits, {total['cache_misses']} misses. "
            "Retrieval-only variants reuse cached trees and cost one reader call per question; "
            "re-running a finished config costs nothing.\n"
        )
        parts.append(
            "## Runs\n\n| Run id | Split | Method | Chunking | Clustering | Retrieval | Embedding |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"
        )
        for r in runs:
            f = r.get("factors", {})
            parts.append(
                f"| `{r['run_id']}` | {r['split']} | {r['method']} | {f.get('chunking', '')} "
                f"| {f.get('clustering', '')} | {f.get('retrieval', '')} | {f.get('embedding', '')} |\n"
            )

    path = out_dir / "README.md"
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")
    return path

parsed.module_docstring:
Run QuALITY experiments from YAML configs.

An experiment file is a :class:`ExperimentConfig`: a :class:`~raptor.config.RaptorConfig`
under ``raptor:`` plus eval settings (split, method, top-k / budget overrides, embedding
shorthand). Each config hashes to a run id; results go to ``artifacts/runs/<run_id>/``::

    config.yaml     the experiment config (as run)
    results.jsonl   one row per question (appended as questions finish)
    state.json      resumable progress: cost counters, per-story tree stats and build time
    summary.json    written when every question is answered

Trees are cached under ``artifacts/trees/<article_id>/<fingerprint>/``, keyed by the
sections that shape a tree (chunking, clustering, builder, models), so retrieval-only
variants never rebuild. Every model call goes through the disk cache, so an interrupted
run resumes where it stopped and a finished config can be re-run for free.

def get_or_build(
        self, article: QualityArticle, cfg: RaptorConfig, method: str, models: ModelBundle
    ) -> TreeRecord:
        path = self.path(article.article_id, cfg, method)
        lock = self._locks.setdefault(str(path), threading.Lock())
        with lock:
            meta_file = path / "build.json"
            if meta_file.exists():
                meta = json.loads(meta_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                return TreeRecord(load_tree(path), float(meta["seconds"]), False, meta["stats"])
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            if method == "flat":
                tree = build_leaf_tree(article.article, cfg, models)
            else:
                tree = TreeBuilder(cfg, models.embedding, models.summarization).build_from_text(
                    article.article
                )
            seconds = time.perf_counter() - t0
            tok = default_tokenizer()
            stats = tree_stats(tree, lambda t: len(tok.encode(t, disallowed_special=())))
            save_tree(tree, path)
            meta = {
                "article_id": article.article_id,
                "title": article.title,
                "method": method,
                "seconds": seconds,
                "stats": stats,
                "created_at": _now(),
                "config": {s: cfg.model_dump(mode="json")[s] for s in TREE_SECTIONS},
            }
            meta_file.write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
            logger.info(
                "built %s tree for %s in %.1fs: %d nodes, %d layers",
                method,
                article.article_id,
                seconds,
                len(tree.all_nodes),
                tree.num_layers + 1,
            )
            return TreeRecord(tree, seconds, True, stats)
